name: ctl_003
text:
The drawing shows two ebselen-like units (1,2-benzisoselenazol-3(2H)-one) joined through their nitrogen atoms by an ethylene (CH2CH2) linker.

Each unit is a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring made of the two adjacent aromatic carbons, Se, N and a C=O carbon. Se is bonded to one aromatic carbon and to N. The carbonyl carbon is bonded to the other aromatic carbon and to N. The two N atoms are connected by the two-carbon chain.

SMILES for one unit: O=C1c2ccccc2[Se]N1–

Joining two units through the linker gives: O=C1N(CCN2[Se]c3ccccc3C2=O)[Se]c2ccccc12

Check on the ring closures: C1(=O) opens ring 1, then N(...) carries the linker. The linker CCN2 opens ring 2 on the second N, then [Se]c3ccccc3C2=O closes the second unit, with C2=O bonded back to N2. Back in the first unit, [Se]c2ccccc12 is Se, then the aromatic carbon, then the ring-fusion carbon that closes ring 1 to the carbonyl carbon. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1N(CCN2[Se]c3ccccc3C2=O)[Se]c2ccccc12

name: ctl_002
text:
I read this as carisbamate, the (S)-enantiomer.

- **Carbamate end:** H₂N–C(=O)–O– is attached to a CH₂ group.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH₂ is bonded to a CH carbon that carries an OH on a hashed bond (pointing away from the viewer) and a 2-chlorophenyl ring. The Cl is ortho to the ring carbon attached to this CH.
- **CIP priorities at the stereocentre:** OH ranks first, CH₂O second (O,H,H beats C,C,C), the aryl carbon third, and H fourth.
- **Assignment:** the hashed OH puts the implicit H toward the viewer. Going OH → CH₂ → aryl runs clockwise on the page, so the true sense with H at the back is reversed, giving S.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** in `NC(=O)OC[C@H](O)c1ccccc1Cl` the neighbour order at the centre is CH₂, H, O, aryl, and `@` works out to R. The S configuration therefore needs `@@`.

SMILES: NC(=O)OC[C@@H](O)c1ccccc1Cl

name: ctl_004
text:
The image shows gadopentetate dimeglumine, drawn as separate components:

- **DTPA ligand:** a diethylenetriamine backbone with five CH2COOH arms. Three arms are drawn as carboxylates (O⁻) and two as COOH, which gives a net charge of 3−.
- **Metal ion:** Gd³⁺, which balances the three negative charges.
- **Two meglumine molecules:** each is N-methyl-D-glucamine, CH3-NH-CH2-(CHOH)4-CH2OH, drawn neutral.

For the meglumine stereochemistry, I worked out the CIP configuration of the carbon next to the CH2–N group from the hashed bond in the drawing and found it to be S. The standard (2R,3R,4R,5S) meglumine SMILES gives the same descriptor at that carbon, so I used it for both copies. I did not check the other three stereocentres against the drawing one by one.

SMILES: OC(=O)CN(CC([O-])=O)CCN(CC([O-])=O)CCN(CC(O)=O)CC([O-])=O.[Gd+3].CNC[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@@H](CO)O)O)O)O.CNC[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@@H](CO)O)O)O)O

name: ctl_001
text:
I read this as the 20-residue peptide with sequence D-Phe-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Gly-Gly-Gly-Asn-Gly-Asp-Phe-Glu-Glu-Ile-Pro-Glu-Glu-Tyr-Leu, which is bivalirudin. I traced it from the N-terminal D-Phe (drawn at the right with a free NH2) to the C-terminal Leu (drawn at the left with a free COOH).

- **Backbone:** the four consecutive glycines sit between Pro4 and Asn, as drawn.
- **Side chains:** Arg carries its guanidine group, Asn its primary amide, Asp and the four Glu residues free carboxylic acids, and Tyr a para-hydroxyphenyl group. Ile and Leu carry their alkyl side chains.
- **Stereochemistry:** all residues are L except the N-terminal Phe, which is D. I matched the Pro and Ile chirality tags against standard L-proline and L-isoleucine SMILES.

I did not run a validity check beyond reading the SMILES back against the drawing residue by residue.

SMILES: N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCNC(=N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)O

name: ctl_007
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Isoxazoline ring:** C5 carries the CF3 group and the 3,5-dichlorophenyl ring. It is bonded to O1, which is bonded to N2. N2 is double-bonded to C3, and C3 is bonded to C4 (CH2), which closes the ring back to C5.
- **Central benzene ring:** C3 of the isoxazoline is attached to the benzene ring. A methyl group sits ortho to the carbonyl-bearing carbon, and the isoxazoline is para to that carbonyl carbon.
- **Side chain:** the benzene carries C(=O)NH-CH2-C(=O)NH-CH2CF3.

Writing the SMILES starting from the dichlorophenyl ring: Clc1cc(Cl)cc(c1)C2(C(F)(F)F)CC(=NO2)c3ccc(C(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(F)(F)F)c(C)c3

Checking the benzene ring: c3 (attached to the isoxazoline), then c, c, then c(C(=O)...) para to the attachment, then c(C), then c3 closing the ring. The ring atoms in order are C1 (isoxazoline), C2 (H), C3 (H), C4 (carboxamide), C5 (methyl), C6 (H). The methyl is therefore ortho to the carboxamide and meta to the isoxazoline, which matches the drawing.

No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: Clc1cc(Cl)cc(c1)C2(C(F)(F)F)CC(=NO2)c3ccc(C(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(F)(F)F)c(C)c3

name: ctl_008
text:
The drawing shows a phenyl ketone with a diethylamino group on the alpha carbon, drawn as the hydrochloride salt.

- The benzene ring is attached to a carbonyl carbon (C=O).
- The carbonyl carbon is bonded to a CH carbon that carries a CH3 and an N atom.
- The nitrogen carries two ethyl groups (each drawn as H3C–CH2).
- "HCl" is written separately, so the salt is written as a dot-separated component.
- The alpha carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(C)C(=O)c1ccccc1.Cl

name: ctl_009
text:
The drawing is a straight zigzag chain with a CH3 group at the left end and a carboxylic acid (C=O and OH) at the right end.

Counting the chain carbons one at a time:
- The CH3 carbon at the far left is 1 carbon.
- The zigzag vertices run from x≈178 to x≈1385 at a spacing of about 86 px. That is 14 intervals, so 15 vertices.
- The last vertex (x≈1385) is the carboxyl carbon, which carries the =O and the OH.

The total is 1 + 15 = 16 carbons, with all single bonds except the carboxyl C=O. This is hexadecanoic acid (palmitic acid). There are no stereocentres and no wedges or hashes.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)O

name: ctl_010
text:
This structure is atorvastatin, the (3R,5R) dihydroxy heptanoic acid.

- **Chain:** a carboxylic acid (CH2–COOH) leads to two CH(OH) carbons, then two CH2 groups, ending at the pyrrole nitrogen.
- **Pyrrole substituents:** the nitrogen is attached to the chain. The ring carbons carry isopropyl, a C(=O)NH-phenyl amide, a phenyl, and a 4-fluorophenyl.
- **Stereochemistry:** both OH groups are drawn on wedges. For C3, the priorities are OH > C2 > C4 > H. With H pointing away, OH → C2 → C4 runs clockwise, so C3 is R. C5 has the same arrangement (OH > C4 > C6 > H), so it is also R.

SMILES: CC(C)c1c(C(=O)Nc2ccccc2)c(-c2ccccc2)c(-c2ccc(F)cc2)n1CC[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O)CC(=O)O

name: ctl_005
text:
I read this as a CPI-type cyclopropa[c]pyrrolo[3,2-e]indol-4-one core (the alkylating unit of CC-1065 and duocarmycin analogues). The core carries a methyl ester on the pyrrole and an N-acyl group, which is a 5,6,7-trimethoxyindole-2-carbonyl.

**Core, left to right:**
- The pyrrole ring has an NH, a C2 bearing CO2Me, and a C3–H. It is fused to a six-membered ring that holds the C=O (the cyclohexadienone).
- The spiro quaternary carbon carries the cyclopropane. The cyclopropane is made of that spiro carbon, a CH2, and a CH.
- That CH is also bonded to a CH2 that leads to the acylated ring nitrogen (the pyrrolidine-type ring).
- The ring nitrogen is bonded to the vinyl carbon C=C, which is part of the enone, and to the amide C=O.

**Right-hand unit:** an indole with its NH, linked through C2 to the amide carbonyl, with OMe groups at C5, C6 and C7.

**Stereochemistry:** two hashed bonds are drawn. One runs from the spiro carbon to the cyclopropane CH2. The other runs from the cyclopropane CH to the CH2 attached to nitrogen. Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES gives `[C@H]` for the cyclopropane CH and `[C@@]` for the spiro carbon.

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=CC2=C(N1)C(=O)C=C3N(C(=O)c4cc5cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c5[nH]4)C[C@H]6C[C@@]236

name: ctl_011
text:
The drawing shows a five-carbon chain, which is ornithine (2,5-diaminopentanoic acid).

- **Carboxylic acid end:** the left carbon carries a C=O (labelled O) and an OH (labelled HO), so it is a COOH group.
- **Chain:** from that carbon the chain runs through C2, C3, C4 and C5, and C5 ends in NH2.
- **Alpha carbon (C2):** it carries an NH2 on a hashed bond, so that group points away from the viewer.
- **Stereochemistry:** the implicit hydrogen on C2 points toward the viewer. The priorities are N, then COOH, then the chain carbon C3, then H. Read from the front, N (down) to COOH (upper left) to C3 (upper right) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving S. This matches L-ornithine.
- **SMILES check:** `N[C@@H](CCCN)C(=O)O` uses the same neighbour order as L-alanine, `N[C@@H](C)C(=O)O`, and the priorities are the same, so it also gives S.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CCCN)C(=O)O

name: ctl_012
text:
The drawing shows an N-benzyl-N-methyl amine whose nitrogen is bonded to a CH(CH3)–CH2–phenyl unit, with HCl as a separate component.

- **Left side:** a phenyl ring is attached to a CH2, which connects to the stereocentre CH. The stereocentre carries a methyl group on a wedge bond and is bonded to N.
- **Nitrogen:** N bears a methyl group and a CH2–phenyl (benzyl) group.
- **Salt:** HCl is drawn beside the structure, so I wrote it as `.Cl`.

**Stereochemistry:** The CH3 on the stereocentre is on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CH2Ph > CH3 > H. On the page, N (upper right) → CH2 (upper left) → CH3 (bottom) runs counterclockwise, which gives (S).

For the SMILES `C[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)N(C)Cc1ccccc1`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH3, H, CH2, N. With `@@`, this arrangement corresponds to S, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)N(C)Cc1ccccc1.Cl

name: ctl_015
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with two substituents on opposite carbons (para). One substituent is OH. The other is a nitrogen carrying two CH3 groups (H3C–N–CH3), which is a dimethylamino group. The molecule is 4-(dimethylamino)phenol.

SMILES: CN(C)c1ccc(O)cc1

name: ctl_014
text:
The image shows aspartic acid: a HOOC–CH(NH2)–CH2–COOH chain with one hashed bond to NH2.

**Connectivity:** the left carboxyl is HO–C(=O)–, attached to the α-carbon, which carries NH2. The α-carbon connects to a CH2, which connects to the right carboxyl, –C(=O)OH.

**Stereochemistry:** the NH2 sits on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer. The implicit H therefore points toward the viewer. Viewed from the H side, the sequence COOH (upper left) → CH2 (upper right) → NH2 (bottom) runs clockwise.

Writing the SMILES with the neighbour order COOH, H, N, CH2, this arrangement corresponds to `@@`. This matches the L-configuration of aspartic acid. I confirmed that by comparing with the known L-aspartic SMILES `N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)O`: the two neighbour orderings differ by two swaps, so the tag stays `@@`.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@@H](N)CC(=O)O

name: ctl_017
text:
The drawing shows an indole with a 2-(piperidin-4-yl)ethyl chain on C3.

- **Indole:** the five-membered ring contains an NH, a C2–C3 double bond, and the two fusion carbons. The benzene ring is fused to it.
- **Chain:** two CH2 groups link indole C3 to the piperidine.
- **Piperidine:** a six-membered ring with an NH, attached through its C4, which is the carbon opposite the nitrogen.

There are no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: C1CNCCC1CCc1c[nH]c2ccccc12

name: ctl_018
text:
The drawing shows lansoprazole. Reading it region by region:

- **Benzimidazole:** a benzene ring fused to an imidazole ring with an N and an NH. Carbon 2 of the imidazole carries the sulfoxide.
- **Linker:** the sulfur is drawn as S=O and is bonded to a CH2.
- **Pyridine:** the CH2 attaches at C2 of the pyridine. C3 carries a methyl (CH3). C4 carries the OCH2CF3 group.

The sulfoxide sulfur is a stereocentre by connectivity, but the bonds are plain, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: Cc1c(CS(=O)c2nc3ccccc3[nH]2)nccc1OCC(F)(F)F

SMILES: Cc1c(CS(=O)c2nc3ccccc3[nH]2)nccc1OCC(F)(F)F

name: ctl_013
text:
I read the structure region by region and wrote it as one SMILES.

- **Indole core:** N1 carries an ethyl group. C2 is bonded to a pyridine ring, and C3 carries the macrocyclic chain. C5 of the benzo ring is bonded to the thiazole.
- **Pyridine:** it is attached to the indole at its C3. C2 of the pyridine bears CH(CH3)OCH3, and C5 bears a 4-methylpiperazin-1-yl group.
- **Macrocycle chain:** from indole C3 the chain runs CH2–C(CH3)2–CH2–O–C(=O) to the alpha carbon of a piperazic acid ring. That ring is Cα–CH2–CH2–CH2–N–NH, closing back on Cα. Its acylated ring nitrogen is bonded to C(=O)–CH(NHC(=O)-2-methylcyclopropyl)–CH2, and that CH2 is bonded to C2 of the thiazole.
- **Thiazole:** C4 is bonded to indole C5, and C2 is bonded to the CH2 of the macrocycle chain.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so none is included.

SMILES: CCn1c(-c3cc(N4CCN(C)CC4)cnc3C(C)OC)c(CC(C)(C)COC(=O)C5CCCN(N5)C(=O)C(NC(=O)C6CC6C)Cc7nc(cs7)%11)c2cc%11ccc12

name: ctl_016
text:
I read the molecule as a 5-(trifluoromethoxy)indol-3-yl ketone. The carbonyl carbon is bonded to a single stereocentre, and that carbon carries an NH-aryl group and a 4-chloro-2-methoxyphenyl group.

- **Indole part:** the 1H-indole is attached at C3 to the C=O. It has an OCF3 group at C5.
- **Anilino part:** the NH is bonded to a benzene ring bearing OCH3 and S(=O)(=O)CH3 at the two meta positions (a 3,5-disubstituted ring).
- **Aryl part:** the 4-chloro-2-methoxyphenyl ring is attached directly to the stereocentre.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge or hash in the drawing is a hashed bond from the stereocentre to N, so the N points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - CIP priorities are N > C(=O) > aryl carbon > H.
  - Viewed from the front, N → C=O → aryl runs clockwise. Because the H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is S.
  - In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` with neighbour order C(=O), H, N, aryl corresponds to S.

SMILES: O=C(c1c[nH]c2ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc12)[C@@H](Nc1cc(OC)cc(S(C)(=O)=O)c1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1OC

name: ctl_006
text:
I read the molecule as a 6-chlorooxindole spiro-fused at C3 to a pyrrolidine, which is in turn spiro-fused to a 4,4-dimethylcyclohexane. The pyrrolidine carries a 2-chloro-3-fluoropyridin-4-yl group and a carboxamide. The carboxamide nitrogen is attached to a tetrahydropyran that bears a primary carboxamide.

**Ring systems**
- **Oxindole:** the aromatic ring has Cl at C6, the carbon adjacent to C7, which is next to the NH-bearing carbon. C3 is the spiro carbon.
- **Pyrrolidine:** it has five atoms: NH, the spiro carbon shared with the cyclohexane, the oxindole C3, the CH bearing the pyridine, and the CH bearing the amide carbonyl.
- **Cyclohexane:** the spiro carbon and the CMe2 carbon are three bonds apart in both directions around the ring, so this is a 4,4-dimethylcyclohexane.
- **Pyridine:** C4 is the attachment point, C3 carries F, C2 carries Cl, and N is at position 1.
- **Tetrahydropyran:** the ring is O, CH2, CH(NH-amide), CH2, CH2, CH(CONH2).

**Stereochemistry**
The drawing shows wedges or hashes at five stereocentres:
- the oxindole spiro carbon, wedge to the cyclohexane spiro carbon;
- the pyridine-bearing pyrrolidine CH, hashed;
- the carbonyl-bearing pyrrolidine CH, wedge;
- the tetrahydropyran C–N carbon, wedge;
- the tetrahydropyran C–CONH2 carbon, hashed.

I assigned each @/@@ from the 2D geometry and implicit-H positions. The cyclohexane spiro carbon has two identical ring arms, so it carries no stereo label.

SMILES: O=C1Nc2cc(Cl)ccc2[C@]13C4(CCC(C)(C)CC4)N[C@@H](C(=O)N[C@@H]5CC[C@@H](C(N)=O)OC5)[C@@H]3c6ccnc(Cl)c6F

name: ctl_019
text:
This is meclizine, which has a piperazine ring with two substituents on its nitrogens.

- **Left nitrogen:** it carries a benzyl group. The benzene ring has a methyl at the meta position relative to the CH2. The ring runs from the CH2-bearing carbon (upper right) to the carbon below it, then to the carbon bearing CH3 at the bottom. That puts CH3 meta to the CH2.
- **Right nitrogen:** it carries a CH attached to a 4-chlorophenyl group and a phenyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I include no stereo.

SMILES: Cc1cccc(CN2CCN(CC2)C(c2ccccc2)c2ccc(Cl)cc2)c1

name: ctl_023
text:
The drawing shows a five-membered oxazolidine-2,4-dione ring with these atoms:

- O1 is the ring oxygen.
- C2 is a carbonyl carbon (C=O) bonded to O1 and N3.
- N3 carries a methyl group.
- C4 is a carbonyl carbon (C=O) bonded to N3 and C5.
- C5 is a quaternary carbon bearing both a methyl and an ethyl group, and it closes the ring back to O1.

C5 is a stereocentre by connectivity, but the drawing uses only plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is assigned.

Written as SMILES: CCC1(C)OC(=O)N(C)C1=O. This has the ring atoms O1, C2, N3, C4 and C5, plus the three substituents (N-methyl, C5-methyl, C5-ethyl), which matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CCC1(C)OC(=O)N(C)C1=O

name: ctl_024
text:
Reading the drawing from left to right gives HS–CH2–CH2–CH(NH2)–COOH, which is homocysteine.

- **Chain:** the thiol (HS) sits on the left. Two CH2 carbons follow, then the central CH carbon, then the carboxylic acid carbon with its C=O and OH.
- **Stereocentre:** the only wedge is the bold bond from the central carbon to NH2, so that carbon is the only stereocentre drawn. The CIP priorities are N, then COOH, then CH2, with H pointing away from the viewer. Going from N (bottom) to COOH (upper right) to CH2 (upper left) runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S, which is the L-amino-acid configuration.
- **SMILES check:** `SCC[C@H](N)C(=O)O` lists the neighbours of the stereocentre as CH2, H, N, COOH, and `@` means counterclockwise when viewed from the CH2. This is the same arrangement as the standard L-homocysteine string `N[C@@H](CCS)C(=O)O`, since swapping N and CH2 flips `@@` to `@`.

SMILES: SCC[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: ctl_021
text:
This structure is camptothecin, read region by region as follows.

- **Left lactone ring:** a quaternary carbon carries an ethyl group and an OH drawn on a wedge. It is bonded to a lactone C(=O), which is bonded to O and then CH2.
- **Pyridone ring:** the CH2 attaches to a ring carbon that bonds to the C=O of the pyridone (C(=O)–N). The other ring carbon bonds back to the quaternary carbon, and the ring continues through a CH to the carbon bonded to N.
- **Five-membered ring:** the pyridone N connects through a CH2 to the quinoline carbon.
- **Quinoline unit:** it contains the aromatic N and the fused benzo ring.

Stereochemistry: only the one stereocentre is drawn with a wedge. With the OH toward the viewer, the ethyl, ring carbon and lactone C=O run clockwise when viewed from the OH side. In the SMILES neighbour order (ethyl, ring-closure carbon, OH, lactone C=O) this corresponds to `@@`, which gives the (S) configuration.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCc2c1cc1-c3nc4ccccc4cc3Cn1c2=O

name: ctl_026
text:
The drawing shows a naphthalene-1,4-dione core (a benzene ring fused to a quinone ring) with a methyl group on C2. This is menadione (vitamin K3).

Reading the quinone ring:
- C1 at the top, drawn as C=O with the O at upper left, is bonded to C2.
- C2 carries the H3C group and has a double bond to C3, which is drawn as CH.
- C3 is bonded to C4, which is drawn as C=O with the O at lower right.
- C4 and C1 connect through the fused benzene ring.

SMILES: CC1=CC(=O)c2ccccc2C1=O

SMILES: CC1=CC(=O)c2ccccc2C1=O

name: ctl_022
text:
This structure is SN-38 (7-ethyl-10-hydroxycamptothecin), read from the drawing as follows.

- **Core:** a camptothecin-type pentacyclic skeleton. It has a quinoline unit fused to a five-membered ring containing N, then a pyridone, then a lactone.
- **Substituents:** an ethyl group on the quinoline carbon next to the ring fusion, and an OH on the benzo ring, separated from the ring-fusion carbon by one CH.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries an ethyl group, a hashed OH, the lactone C=O and the ring carbon.

For the stereocentre, I assigned CIP priorities as OH > lactone C(=O)O > ring carbon > ethyl. With the OH hashed (pointing back) and the ethyl in the plane, this gives the S configuration, which matches natural camptothecin. In the SMILES the neighbour order at that carbon is lactone C, ring-closure carbon, OH, ethyl, and `[C@]` encodes S for that order.

SMILES: CCC1=C2CN3C(=CC4=C(C3=O)COC(=O)[C@]4(O)CC)C2=NC2=CC=C(O)C=C12

name: ctl_028
text:
The drawing shows a central Hg atom bonded to two CH3 groups, one on each side (H3C–Hg–CH3). This is dimethylmercury. Both bonds are plain single bonds, and there are no stereocentres or charges.

SMILES: C[Hg]C

name: ctl_025
text:
The drawing is captopril, (2S)-1-[(2S)-3-mercapto-2-methylpropanoyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid. I read it in three parts.

- **Acyl chain:** HS–CH2–CH(CH3)–C(=O)–, attached to the ring nitrogen through the carbonyl carbon. The methyl group on the chain carbon is drawn with a hashed bond.
- **Ring:** a five-membered pyrrolidine made of N and four carbons. The carbon next to N carries a COOH group on a hashed bond.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned CIP descriptors from the hashed bonds.
  - Methyl-bearing carbon: the priorities are CH2SH > C(=O)N > CH3 > H. With the methyl hashed (away from the viewer), the H points toward the viewer. This gives S.
  - Ring carbon: the priorities are N > COOH > ring CH2 > H. With the COOH hashed, the H again points toward the viewer. This gives S, which is the natural L-proline configuration.

I then checked that the SMILES below encodes S at both centres, which it does.

SMILES: C[C@H](CS)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: ctl_029
text:
The drawing shows creatine. Reading it region by region:

- **Carboxylic acid:** a carbon with a C=O (labeled O) and an OH (labeled HO).
- **Linker:** a CH2 joins the carboxyl carbon to a nitrogen.
- **Nitrogen:** it carries a methyl group (CH3) and is also bonded to the guanidine carbon.
- **Guanidine carbon:** it has a C=NH double bond and a single bond to NH2.

All bonds are plain, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: OC(=O)CN(C)C(=N)N

name: ctl_031
text:
This is mersalyl sodium, drawn as separate ions: Na+, the organomercury cation, and hydroxide.

Reading the organic part from the drawing:
- The carboxylate is O⁻–C(=O)–CH2–O, with the CH2 attached to an ether oxygen on the benzene ring.
- The benzene ring carries the OCH2COO⁻ group and, on the adjacent carbon, a C(=O)NH amide group (ortho substitution).

- Anion and chain: [O-]C(=O)COc1ccccc1C(=O)NCC(OC)C[Hg+]
- Counterions: [Na+] and [OH-]

Charge check: Na+ (+1), Hg+ (+1), carboxylate (−1) and hydroxide (−1) sum to zero.

The only potential stereocentre is the CH bearing OMe, and it is drawn with plain bonds, so I added no stereo.

SMILES: [Na+].[O-]C(=O)COc1ccccc1C(=O)NCC(OC)C[Hg+].[OH-]

name: ctl_032

name: ctl_027
text:
This is tetracycline hydrochloride, and I wrote the SMILES from memory of tetracycline's standard stereo SMILES rather than deriving each centre from the drawing's wedges and hashes.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Next ring:** a carbon bearing a methyl and an OH (the methyl drawn hashed), then a ring-fusion carbon, and an enolised carbon bearing OH that joins the aromatic ring.
- **Third ring:** a ketone (C=O), a carbon bearing OH (drawn hashed), and a CH2 bridge shown with wedge bonds.
- **Right ring:** an enol OH, a carboxamide (C(=O)NH2), a ketone, and a CH bearing N(CH3)2 (drawn hashed).

name: ctl_034
text:
The drawing shows fluconazole.

- **Central carbon:** a quaternary carbon bearing an OH, a 2,4-difluorophenyl ring, and two CH2 groups.
- **Triazole rings:** each CH2 is attached to N1 of a 1,2,4-triazole. In the top ring, N1 is bonded to N2, which is bonded to C3, then N4, then C5. The ring in the lower right has the same connectivity.

name: ctl_035
text:
The image shows a linear decapeptide: pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑D‑Ser(tBu)‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑NHEt, which is buserelin. I read it residue by residue from the pyroglutamate end:

5. The C‑terminus is Pro as an N‑ethylamide (C(=O)NHCH2CH3).

name: ctl_036
text:
I read the structure in four parts and then fixed the double-bond geometry from the drawing.

- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring with CF3 groups at both meta positions (a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group), attached to C3 of a 1,2,4-triazole.
- **Triazole:** its N1 is bonded to a vinyl CH. The ring order is N1, C5(H), N4, C3(aryl), N2.

- **Pyrimidine:** a six-membered ring with nitrogens at positions 1 and 3, attached through C5.

For the geometry, the triazole N and the pyrimidine both sit below the C=C axis in the drawing, so they are cis. The amide is therefore trans to the triazole N, which gives `NC(=O)/C(...)=C/n1...`. The drawing shows no other stereocentres.

name: ctl_020
text:
This is dirithromycin, a 14-membered azalide-type macrolide. I read it region by region and then worked out each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes; I did not check the result against a database entry.

**Macrolactone ring:**
- The lactone carbonyl (C=O) sits next to an α-carbon bearing a methyl.
- Next come a carbon bearing the cladinose O-link, then a methyl-bearing carbon.
- Then a carbon bearing the desosamine O-link, then a quaternary C(OH)(CH3), then CH2.
- Then a CH(CH3), then a CH–N, then a CH(CH3), then a CH–O.
- Then a quaternary C(OH)(CH3), then CH(ethyl)–O, which closes the lactone.

**Fused oxazine ring:**
- A six-membered ring is formed by NH, CH, O and three macrocycle carbons.
- Its CH carries a CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH3 side chain.

**Left sugar (cladinose-type):**
- A pyranose with an anomeric O-link, a CH2, a quaternary C(CH3)(OCH3), a CH–OH and a CH(CH3)–O ring closure.

**Bottom sugar (desosamine-type):**
- A pyranose with an anomeric O-link, a CH–OH, a CH–N(CH3)2, a CH2 and a CH(CH3)–O ring closure.

**Stereochemistry:** wedges and hashes were read bond by bond at every drawn stereocentre. The anomeric hash on the desosamine O-link is ambiguous in the drawing, and I assumed it starts at the anomeric carbon.

name: ctl_033
text:
I read the drawing as a 17-hydroxy-androstan-3-one skeleton with an extra methyl on C1, and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash.

**Skeleton and substituents**

- C1 carries a methyl on a wedge.
- C10 carries a methyl on a hash.
- C13 carries a methyl on a hash.

name: ctl_037
text:
This structure is midazolam: an imidazo[1,5-a][1,4]benzodiazepine core carrying a 1-methyl group, a chlorine on the benzo ring and a 2-fluorophenyl substituent.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Imidazole ring:** the methyl-bearing carbon (CH3) sits between the ring N (drawn as "N" at the left) and the bridgehead N. The ring atoms are C(CH3), N, CH, a carbon bonded to the CH2, and the bridgehead N. The double bonds are C(CH3)=N and CH=C.
- **Diazepine ring:** the CH2 joins the imidazole carbon to the imine N. That N is double-bonded to the carbon bearing the 2-fluorophenyl group, which bonds to the benzo ring. The benzo ring bonds to the bridgehead N.
- **Benzo ring:** the carbon attached to the C=N carbon is adjacent to the CH that is adjacent to the C–Cl carbon. The chlorine is para to the bridgehead-N-bearing carbon, which is consistent with midazolam's 8-chloro position.
- **Fluorophenyl ring:** F is on the carbon ortho to the attachment point.

Writing this as SMILES:

Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(=NC2)c1ccccc1F

Atom check: in the SMILES, the benzo ring runs c1 (attached to N), c, c, c(Cl), c, c1 (attached to C=N). The carbon bearing Cl is therefore para to the N-bearing carbon, which matches the drawing, where the C–Cl carbon is the bottom-right vertex. The ring is N-c(a), then bottom-left, bottom, bottom-right (Cl), top-right, and top-left (attached to C=N), and the Cl carbon is three bonds from the N-bearing carbon, so it is para. This is correct.

SMILES: Cc1ncc2CN=C(c3ccccc3F)c3cc(Cl)ccc3-n12

name: ctl_030
text:
I read this as lasalocid A and worked out each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Skeleton, left to right:**
- A tetrahydropyran ring carries an ethyl and a hydroxyl on one carbon and a methyl on the adjacent carbon.
- Its other α-carbon is bonded to a tetrahydrofuran ring that has an ethyl on the quaternary carbon, a methyl on the next ring carbon, and an exocyclic CH on the carbon next to the ring oxygen.

- The chain ends on an aromatic ring bearing COOH, OH and CH₃ in the 1,2,3 pattern drawn.

**Stereo:** I assigned @/@@ at each wedge or hash centre by looking at which substituent points toward or away from the viewer. I then converted that to SMILES neighbour order by counting permutation parity. The stereo marks come from my own reading of the drawing and were not checked against a reference structure.

name: ctl_043
text:
This image shows two separate components, which is ciclopirox olamine (the ethanolamine salt of ciclopirox).

**Component 1 (ciclopirox):** a pyridin-2-one ring.

name: ctl_040
text:
This is micafungin, and I wrote the SMILES from the drawing's connectivity. I recalled the stereodescriptors from the known structure rather than deriving each one from the wedges, so they are the least certain part.

**Side chain (left):** a pentyloxy-substituted phenyl ring (CH3(CH2)4–O–C6H4) is attached to C5 of an isoxazole. C3 of the isoxazole is bonded to a para-substituted phenyl ring. That ring carries a C(=O)NH– amide that links to the macrocycle.

name: ctl_038
text:
I read the structure as a spiro-fused oxindole-type amide linked to a substituted piperidinone, and assigned the stereo SMILES from the wedge and hash bonds.

**Fragments**
- **Spiro core:** a 2-oxo-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine (7-azaoxindole) is spiro-fused at its C3 to a 6,7-dihydro-5H-cyclopenta[b]pyridine.
- **Linker:** a carboxamide, C(=O)NH, sits on the pyridine ring of the cyclopenta[b]pyridine, para to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to the CH2.

- **Aryl group:** a 2,3,6-trifluorophenyl on C5. The fluorines sit on the ortho carbon on each side of the attachment carbon and on the carbon next to one of them.

- **Spiro carbon:** the hashed bond goes to the CH2 on the pyridine side, which gives `[C@]13`.
- **Piperidinone C3:** the hashed NH gives `[C@@H]`.
- **Piperidinone C6:** the hashed methyl gives `[C@H]`.
- **Piperidinone C5:** the hashed aryl gives `[C@H]`.

I checked the SMILES for valid ring closures and atom counts against the drawing.

text:
I read the image as the decapeptide pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑D‑Trp‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑NHEt. This matches the GnRH analogue deslorelin, though I worked it out from the drawing rather than by recognising the name.

**Residues, N‑terminus to C‑terminus:**
- **pGlu:** a 5‑oxopyrrolidine ring whose carbonyl carbon is attached to His.
- **His:** an imidazole side chain on a CH2.
- **Trp (upper):** an indole side chain.
- **Ser:** a CH2OH side chain.
- **Tyr:** a 4‑hydroxyphenyl side chain.
- **Trp (lower):** an indole side chain.
- **Leu:** an isobutyl side chain.
- **Arg:** a guanidine‑terminated propyl side chain.
- **Pro:** a pyrrolidine ring, capped at the C‑terminus as an N‑ethyl amide (C(=O)NHCH2CH3).

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each α‑carbon from the wedge or hash on its carbonyl bond and the positions of its three drawn neighbours, with the implicit H on the opposite face.
- pGlu, His, upper Trp, Ser, Tyr, Leu, Arg and Pro all come out S, i.e. the L configuration.

name: ctl_044
text:
This structure is benidipine, a 1,4-dihydropyridine bearing a methyl ester, an N-benzylpiperidin-3-yl ester and a 3-nitrophenyl group.

**Reading the drawing**
- **Dihydropyridine core:** an N–H ring with a methyl on each carbon next to nitrogen (C2 and C6).
- **C3 and C5 esters:** a methyl ester on one and an ester to the piperidine oxygen on the other.
- **C4 substituent:** a 3-nitrophenyl group, drawn on a solid wedge.
- **Piperidine:** a six-membered ring with N-benzyl, attached through C3 by a hashed bond to the ester oxygen.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Piperidine C3:** the oxygen is on a hash, so the implicit hydrogen points toward the viewer. The priorities are O > C2 (attached to N) > C4 > H. O → C2 → C4 runs counterclockwise from the front, which reverses to clockwise with H pointing toward the viewer. This gives R, which is `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order used.
- **Dihydropyridine C4:** the aryl group is wedged, so H points away from the viewer. The priorities are the ring carbon bearing the piperidinyl ester > the ring carbon bearing the methyl ester > aryl > H. Going from upper-left to upper-right to the aryl at the bottom is clockwise, which gives R. This is `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order used.

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)O[C@@H]2CCCN(Cc3ccccc3)C2)[C@@H]1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: ctl_046
text:
The structure is a pregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione steroid. This matches beclomethasone: 9-chloro-11β,17,21-trihydroxy-16β-methylpregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione.

- **Ring A:** a cross-conjugated dienone, with a C3 ketone and C1=C2 and C4=C5 double bonds.
- **C10 and C13:** each carries an angular methyl group, drawn with a wedge.
- **C9:** carries Cl, drawn with a hash (α).
- **C11:** carries OH, drawn with a wedge (β).
- **C16:** carries a methyl group, drawn with a wedge (β).
- **C17:** carries OH, drawn with a hash (α), and the side chain C(=O)CH2OH.

I wrote the SMILES from this reading and took the stereo descriptors from the standard beclomethasone SMILES as I remember it. I did not rederive each @/@@ from the drawing. The hashed bond near C8 is drawn unusually, so the stereo at that centre rests on the standard form.

name: ctl_047
text:
The image shows cenobamate: a 2-chlorophenyl ring and a tetrazol-2-yl group on an ethyl carbamate chain.

**Fragments**
- The ring on the left has four N atoms and one C. The ring N bonded to the CH2 is flanked by one N above (the N=N pair at the top left) and one N below, which is bonded to the ring CH. This makes it a 2-substituted 2H-tetrazole, written `Cn1nncn1`.
- The CH2 is attached to the stereocentre.
- The stereocentre carries an O–C(=O)–NH2 carbamate on the right, and the 2-chlorophenyl ring on a hashed bond.
- The benzene ring has Cl on the carbon adjacent to the one bonded to the stereocentre (ortho).

**Stereochemistry**
- The CIP priorities at the stereocentre are O > CH2–N > aryl C > H.
- The aryl bond is hashed (pointing away), so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- Going O (right), then CH2 (upper left), then aryl (lower left) is counterclockwise in the drawing. Because H faces the viewer, this reverses to clockwise, which is R.
- In SMILES, `O[C@@H](Cn1nncn1)c1ccccc1Cl` gives R for this neighbour order.

name: ctl_048
text:
The drawing shows a 10,11-dihydro-5H-dibenzo[a,d]cycloheptene core with an imidazol-1-yl group on C5 and two chlorines on one benzo ring.

**Core.** The left benzene ring is unsubstituted. The seven-membered ring contains the CH2CH2 bridge at the top and the CH carrying the imidazole at the bottom. The right benzene ring is fused to the seven-membered ring.

**Right ring.** Its vertices are:
- C_a (808,620), attached to the CH2
- C (908,620), a CH
- C (958,706), bearing Cl
- C (908,792), a CH
- C (808,792), bearing Cl
- C_b (758,706), attached to the CH(N)

The Cl at (808,792) sits on the carbon adjacent to C_b, which is the carbon next to the ring fusion on the CH(N) side. The other Cl is on the carbon para to C_b's neighbour, i.e. meta to C_a.

**Imidazole.** It is attached through N1. N1 connects to CH=CH and to a CH that is double-bonded to the second N (N3), which closes the ring.

**SMILES.** Starting from the CH carrying the imidazole:

C1(n2ccnc2)c3ccccc3CCc4cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c14

Checking the right ring in this SMILES: c4 (C_a), c (CH), c(Cl), c (CH), c(Cl), c14 (C_b). This matches the drawing, with C_b closing back to the CH and the Cl on the carbon adjacent to C_b.

SMILES: Clc1cc2CCc3ccccc3C(n3ccnc3)c2c(Cl)c1

name: ctl_045
text:
I read the drawing as the sodium salt of a penicillanic acid sulfone (a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine S,S-dioxide).

**Core**
- The β-lactam has a C=O at C7, its nitrogen is N4, and C6 carries an exocyclic C=C.
- The sulfur is drawn with two S=O groups.
- The ring carbon next to the nitrogen (C3) carries a carboxylate (COO⁻) and the sodium counter-ion is shown separately.

- C5 has a bold wedge to H.
- C2 has the methyl on a hash.
- Reading the wedges and hashes onto the SMILES atom order gives `[C@@H]` at C3, `[C@@H]` at C5 and `[C@@]` at C2.
- In the drawing the pyridyl group lies on the same side of the C6=C double bond as C5, so it is trans to the C7 carbonyl. I encoded this as `C(=O)/C(=C/c3ccccn3)`.

I checked that the ring closures and branches in the SMILES match the atoms in the drawing.

name: ctl_052
text:
The drawing shows a macrocycle with five O atoms, which I located at the top left, top right, right, bottom, and left.

Between neighbouring oxygens I counted the vertices along each bond path:

- Top left O to top right O: one path with two carbons (the vertices at 700,498 and 800,498).
- Top right O to right O: two carbons (958,614 and 989,710).
- Right O to bottom O: two carbons (928,895 and 848,954).

name: ctl_050
text:
The drawing looks like a pantoprazole isomer, so I read it region by region.

**Pyridine ring.** N is at the top. Going around the ring from N: C2 carries the CH2 linker, C3 carries an OMe (the lower methoxy), C4 carries an OMe (the left methoxy), then C5 and C6 are plain CH. This gives a 3,4-dimethoxypyridin-2-yl group, as in pantoprazole.

**Linker.** The pyridine C2 connects to CH2, then to S(=O), then to C2 of the benzimidazole.

**Benzimidazole.** The imidazole ring has one =N and one NH. The benzene ring carries OCHF2 on the carbon at the lower right, which is attached to the ring carbon next to the one bonded to NH.

Tracing the ring atoms:
- The C2 carbon is bonded to N (top) and NH (bottom).
- The top N attaches to C3a, the upper ring-fusion carbon. Moving clockwise along the top, C3a is followed by CH, then CH, then the C–OCHF2 carbon, then CH, then C7a (the lower fusion carbon, attached to NH).
- The OCHF2 carbon is therefore bonded to a CH that is bonded to C7a. Its position is next-but-one from C7a, which makes it C5 or C6.

Written as SMILES, with the NH-bearing fusion carbon c2 and the ring running c2 → cH → c(OCHF2) → cH → cH → c(N=):

`COc1ccnc(CS(=O)c2nc3ccc(OC(F)F)cc3[nH]2)c1OC`

Checking this against the drawing: after the nc3 (the fusion carbon attached to =N) come c, c, then c(OCHF2), then c, then c3 attached to [nH]. So the OCHF2 carbon is separated from the NH-side fusion carbon by one CH, which matches the drawing, where the substituent carbon is adjacent to the CH next to the NH-bearing fusion carbon.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(CS(=O)c2nc3ccc(OC(F)F)cc3[nH]2)c1OC

name: ctl_066

- C2' is R.

name: ctl_064
text:
I read this as colistin A (polymyxin E1). The SMILES below follows the drawing's connectivity, but the stereocentres were assigned by assuming the natural configurations rather than checking each wedge and hash.

**Stereochemistry.**
- I took L-Dab, L-Thr and L-Leu as the natural configurations.
- The drawing's hashed bond to the first Leu (position 6) marks it as D-Leu.
- The 6-methyl centre on the fatty acid works out as (S) in my SMILES.

name: ctl_069
text:
This is alectinib, read from the drawing as follows.

**Core.** A benzo[b]carbazole: a benzene ring fused to a six-membered ring that carries the C=O and the gem-dimethyl carbon, which is fused to the indole.
- The ketone carbon is bonded to the indole C3.
- The indole C2 is bonded to the quaternary C(CH3)2.
- The indole N-H sits between C2 and the benzo ring.
- The nitrile is on the indole benzo ring, para to the C3a ring-fusion carbon... more precisely, on the carbon adjacent to the CH that neighbors the carbon bearing N.

**Left ring.** Its substituents are an ethyl group and a 4-morpholinopiperidin-1-yl group (the piperidine N attaches to the ring, and the piperidine C4 carries the morpholine N).

**SMILES construction.**
- Start with the ethyl-bearing aromatic carbon: CCc1cc2c(cc1N1CCC(CC1)N1CCOCC1)C(C)(C)c1[nH]c3cc(C#N)ccc3c1C2=O
- Left ring: c1 (ethyl-bearing), then cH, then c2 (bonded to C=O), then c (bonded to CMe2), then cH, then c1 (bearing the piperidine N). This matches the drawing: the ethyl carbon is next to a CH, which is next to the ring-fusion carbon bearing C=O, and the piperidine carbon is next to a CH, which is next to the ring-fusion carbon bearing CMe2.
- Indole: c1[nH]c3cc(C#N)ccc3c1. The carbon bonded to N is c3, followed by cH, then c(C#N), then cH, cH, and the ring-fusion c3 bonded to the ketone-side carbon c1. In the drawing, the C-CN carbon is adjacent to a CH that neighbors the C-N carbon, which agrees.

name: ctl_063
text:
I read this as a β-D-glucosyl ceramide built on a C18 phytosphingosine base with an N-linked hexacosanoyl (C26) chain. The stereochemistry is assigned from the known natural configuration, not read from individual wedges.

**Parts of the structure**
- **Sugar head group:** a six-membered ring (pyranose) with a CH2OH at C5 and OH groups at C2, C3 and C4. The wedges and hashes match β-D-glucose, which is attached through the ring oxygen at C1 to the sphingoid C1 (an O-glycoside).
- **Sphingoid base:** C1 (CH2–O), C2 (carrying NH), C3 (OH) and C4 (OH) form the polar head. The chain continues from C4 to a terminal CH3 at the right. Counting zigzag vertices gives 14 carbons after C4, so the base is C18, consistent with phytosphingosine.
- **Acyl chain:** the amide carbonyl sits at the left of the sphingoid head and runs out to the H3C end. From the vertex spacing I counted 26 carbons including the carbonyl, so the acyl group is hexacosanoyl. This count is the least certain part of the reading.

**Stereochemistry:** wedge/hash bonds are drawn at the sphingoid C2, C3 and C4 and at the sugar ring carbons. I took them to be the natural 2S,3S,4R base and β-D-glucose, and wrote the chirality tags to match that.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCC[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](CO[C@H]1[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O1)CO)O)O)O)NC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC

name: ctl_072
text:
The drawing is a heptamethine cyanine dye (an indocyanine green-type sodium salt) with two benzo[e]indole end groups. I read it region by region as follows.

- **End groups:** each side is a 1,1-dimethyl-benzo[e]indole. The gem-dimethyl carbon is bonded to the aromatic carbon that sits next to the ring-fusion carbon of the second benzo ring, which gives the benzo[e] fusion pattern.
- **Nitrogens:** the left nitrogen carries the + charge and is drawn as an iminium (C2=N⁺). The right nitrogen is neutral and the right C2 is exocyclic to the chain. Both nitrogens carry a 4-sulfonatobutyl chain, CCCC–S(=O)(=O)O⁻.
- **Polyene bridge:** counting vertices between the two C2 atoms gives 7 carbons. The double bonds fall as C1=C2, C3=C4, C5=C6 and C7=C2′ (the right-hand ring carbon). I marked the interior double bonds as trans because the chain is drawn as a zigzag.
- **Counter-ion:** Na⁺ is drawn separately. The net charge is +1 (N⁺) −2 (two sulfonates) +1 (Na⁺) = 0, so the structure is balanced.

SMILES: CC1(C)C(/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C2\N(CCCCS(=O)(=O)[O-])c3ccc4ccccc4c3C2(C)C)=[N+](CCCCS(=O)(=O)[O-])c2ccc3ccccc3c12.[Na+]

name: ctl_070
text:
This drawing is esomeprazole magnesium: two (S)-omeprazole anions with one Mg²⁺. I identified it as esomeprazole from the overall layout and the single hashed S–CH₂ bond. name: ctl_075
text:
I read the structure as a venetoclax-type BCL-2 inhibitor in which the usual dimethylcyclohexene is replaced by a spiro[3.5]nonene.

**Regions of the drawing**
- **Left end:** a cyclobutane is spiro-fused to a cyclohexene. The ring double bond carries a 4-chlorophenyl group on one carbon and a CH2 link to the piperazine on the other.
- **Centre:** the piperazine joins a benzamide ring at the para position to the carbonyl. The ortho position carries an O-linked 1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridin-5-yl group.
- **Acyl sulfonamide:** the amide nitrogen is bonded to a sulfonyl group (C(=O)NS(=O)(=O)) that sits on a second benzene ring. That ring has a nitro group ortho to an NH-CH2 substituent.
- **Right end:** the CH2 leads to the 2-position of a 1,4-dioxane ring. The hashed bond to that ring carbon is the only stereo marker in the drawing.

**Stereochemistry**
The stereocentre is the dioxane C2. I took the hashed CH2 as pointing away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are ring O > ring CH2–O > CH2–N > H. Viewed from the front, O → ring CH2 → CH2N runs clockwise, and the H points toward the viewer, so the configuration is S. In the SMILES below, `NC[C@H]3COCCO3` encodes S.

I could not tell from the image which end of the hash is the narrow one. I assumed the narrow end is at the stereocentre, as is usual.

Check: this SMILES is not valid as written, because I garbled the spiro ring. The cyclohexene should be C3=C(Ar)CC4(CCC3)... with the ring closing on the ring atoms, which gives a six-membered ring (C3, C(Ar), CH2, spiro C, CH2, CH2) but the cyclobutane written as CCC4 is a six-atom path in the wrong place. The corrected spiro fragment is below.

SMILES: O=C(NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(NC[C@H]2COCCO2)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1)c1ccc(N2CCN(CC3=C(c4ccc(Cl)cc4)CC4(CCC4)CC3)CC2)cc1Oc1cnc2[nH]ccc2c1

Reading the structure region by region:

text:

- **Middle ring:** a second saturated ring joining the cyclohexane to the benzene through two CH2 groups.
- **Right ring:** a benzene ring bearing SO3⁻ and an isopropyl group on adjacent carbons.
- **Counter-ion:** Na⁺.

I assigned the @/@@ marks from the wedge geometry at each of the three stereocentres. The chain atoms and the sulfonate and sodium charges are as drawn.

name: ctl_121
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left ring:** a six-membered lactam. Going around from the ring nitrogen, the atoms are N, C(=O), CH2, CH2, CF2, CH2. This is a 5,5-difluoropiperidin-2-one.
- **Chain:** the lactam N is bonded to CH2, then to a CH carrying NH2 on a hashed bond, then to CH2, then to C(=O), which is bonded to the ring nitrogen of the right-hand bicycle.
- **Right bicycle:** a 5,6,7,8-tetrahydropyrido[3,4-d]pyrimidine. The saturated ring nitrogen is acylated by the chain carbonyl. The pyrimidine carbons at positions 2 and 4 each carry a CF3 group.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH bearing NH2 has the NH2 on a hash, so the H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are NH2 > CH2–N(lactam) > CH2–C(=O) > H. Viewed from the front, NH2 (bottom), CH2N (upper left), CH2CO (upper right) run clockwise. With H toward the viewer this reverses, so the centre is S. In the SMILES below, the neighbour order at that atom is CH2N, H, N, CH2CO, and `@@` corresponds to S.

SMILES: O=C1CCC(F)(F)CN1C[C@@H](N)CC(=O)N2CCc3c(C(F)(F)F)nc(C(F)(F)F)nc3C2

name: ctl_123
text:

- C2 carries CH3.
- C3 carries the isopropyl ester, C(=O)OC(C)C.
- C4 carries the 3-nitrophenyl group.
- C5 carries the ester C(=O)O–azetidin-3-yl, where the azetidine nitrogen bears a benzhydryl group (CH(Ph)2).
- C6 carries NH2.

The ring is N1H–C2(CH3)=C3–C4H(Ar)–C5=C6(NH2)–N1. I read the double bonds as C2=C3 and C5=C6, which matches the drawing.

The 3-nitrophenyl is attached at the ring carbon with the nitro group meta to it. The nitro group is drawn charge-separated, as [N+](=O)[O-]. No wedges or hashes are shown, so I included no stereochemistry.

SMILES assembled in pieces:

- Check: N1, then C(N)= is C6 with NH2, then C5 with the ester to the azetidine, then C4 with the aryl, then C3 with the isopropyl ester, =C1C is C2 with CH3. This matches the drawing.

name: ctl_124
text:
The drawing is eletriptan hydrobromide.

- **Indole core:** an indole with a free N–H. Its C3 carries a CH2 that links to the pyrrolidine, and its C5 carries a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Side chain:** the C5 chain ends in a sulfonyl group (S with two =O) bonded to a phenyl ring.
- **Pyrrolidine:** an N-methylpyrrolidine, attached through its C2 to the CH2 that goes to indole C3.
- **Stereochemistry:** the single wedge is on the bond from pyrrolidine C2 to the exocyclic CH2, with the narrow end at C2. The CIP priorities at C2 are N, then the exocyclic CH2, then the ring CH2, then H. Viewed with H pointing away, N → exocyclic CH2 → ring CH2 runs clockwise, so the centre is R. The SMILES chirality tag `[C@@H]` as written gives this R configuration.
- **Salt:** the HBr is written as a separate `Br` component.

name: ctl_122
text:
This structure is octreotide acetate: the cyclic octapeptide D-Phe-Cys-Phe-D-Trp-Lys-Thr-Cys-Thr(ol), joined by a Cys–Cys disulfide bridge, with two acetic acid molecules as the salt.

I read the sequence from the ring:
- The N-terminal D-Phe carries a free NH2 and a benzyl side chain.
- The first Cys leads into an L-Phe with a benzyl side chain.
- Next is a D-Trp with an indole side chain, then a Lys with a 4-aminobutyl side chain.
- Then comes a Thr with a CH(OH)CH3 side chain, followed by the second Cys that closes the disulfide.
- The C-terminus is a threoninol, which has a CH2OH instead of a carboxyl group.

For stereochemistry I used the standard octreotide configuration (D-Phe, L-Cys, L-Phe, D-Trp, L-Lys, L-Thr, L-Cys, 2R,3R-threoninol) rather than deriving every centre from the individual wedges and hashes. I checked the Thr stereo descriptors by hand against the known L-threonine SMILES. The threoninol centres are carried over from L-Thr, since reduction to the alcohol does not change the spatial arrangement.

The disulfide is written as a ring closure (`%10`) between the two sulfur atoms.

SMILES: N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS%10)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS%10)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)CO.CC(=O)O.CC(=O)O

name: ctl_126
text:
Reading the drawing gives a thioxanthene core: two benzene rings bridged by an S atom, with a Cl on the lower ring. The central carbon (C9) carries an exocyclic double bond to a CH. name: ctl_129

name: ctl_128
text:
I read this as acalabrutinib, with the stereocentre drawn as (S).

**Fragments read from the drawing:**
- **Propynoyl group:** CH3–C≡C–C(=O)– on the pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- **Pyrrolidine:** a five-membered ring (N plus four carbons).
- **Core:** an imidazo[1,5-a]pyrazine. The pyrrolidine C2 is attached to the imidazole carbon next to the bridgehead N. The aryl group is on the other imidazole carbon, and NH2 is on the pyrazine carbon next to the ring fusion.

**Stereochemistry:** The pyrrolidine C2 has a hashed bond to the imidazole carbon, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > imidazole C > ring CH2 > H. In the image, N (up), then imidazole C (right), then CH2 (lower left) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. In the SMILES below, `[C@H]` written as `N1CCC[C@H]1c…` encodes S, so the two agree.

name: ctl_115
text:
I read this as a vancomycin-type glycopeptide and wrote the SMILES region by region from the drawing.

- **Left side chain:** an N-methylleucine is acylated onto the amino group of the first β-hydroxy-chlorotyrosine. That residue is linked through its C=O to the NH of an asparagine, which carries a CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain.
- **Central ring:** a trisubstituted benzene bears the O-glucose in the middle, an aryl ether to the left chlorophenyl ring and one to the right chlorophenyl ring. Its benzylic CH is bonded to the Asn-derived NH and to a C(=O)NH leading into the right half.
- **Right half:** two further aryl amino acids (a hydroxyphenylglycine and a dihydroxyphenylglycine) are joined by a biaryl bond and carry a free CO2H. The right chlorotyrosine's benzylic carbon carries an O-linked 4-keto-vancosamine-type sugar (3-amino-3-methyl-4-oxo, 6-methyl).
- **Stereochemistry:** I encoded only the wedges actually drawn. These are the quaternary C(NH2)(CH3) of the amino sugar and, in the glucose, the C5 CH2OH and the C3 OH. The other stereocentres are drawn with plain bonds, so they carry no stereo marks.

I derived the @/@@ signs from the drawn wedge geometry. The ring-closure digits are consistent, and the SMILES was not run through a parser.

name: ctl_130
text:
I read this as iopamidol. The ring is a benzene carrying three iodines, two carboxamide groups and one acylamino group.

- **Ring:** a benzene with iodine at the top-left, top-right and bottom positions. The remaining three positions carry the substituents below.
- **Top substituent:** an NH–C(=O)–CH(OH)–CH3 group, which is a 2-hydroxypropanamide.
- **Lower-left and lower-right substituents:** each is a C(=O)–NH–CH(CH2OH)2 group, the amide of 1,3-dihydroxypropan-2-amine.
- **Stereochemistry:** only the lactamide carbon is drawn with a stereo bond. The methyl is hashed, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit hydrogen points toward the viewer.
- **Assignment:** the priorities are OH, then C(=O)N, then CH3, then H. In the drawing, OH sits upper right, C(=O) below and CH3 upper left, which runs clockwise. With H toward the viewer the sense reverses, so the centre is S.
- **SMILES check:** `C[C@H](O)C(=O)N...` has the order CH3, H, O, C(=O). Swapping H to the front and viewing with H pointing away gives O → C(=O) → CH3 counterclockwise, which is S. This matches the drawing.

The two CH(CH2OH)2 carbons are drawn with plain bonds and are not stereocentres, so they carry no stereo marks.

SMILES: C[C@H](O)C(=O)Nc1c(I)c(C(=O)NC(CO)CO)c(I)c(C(=O)NC(CO)CO)c1I

name: ctl_134
text:
The drawing shows medetomidine: a 2,3-dimethylphenyl ring joined through a CH(CH3) carbon to the 5-position of a 1H-imidazole.

**Benzene ring.** The attachment carbon is at the right (748, 762). Going around the ring:
- The vertex at the top (661, 712) carries a CH3, so it is ortho to the attachment point.
- The next vertex at the upper left (573, 762) carries an H3C group, so it is meta.
- The remaining three vertices are unsubstituted.

This gives a 2,3-dimethylphenyl group.

**Linker.** The attachment carbon connects to a CH that bears a CH3 and the imidazole. The bonds are all plain, so no stereochemistry is assigned.

**Imidazole ring.** The ring atoms are:
- C5 at (918, 762), bonded to the linker carbon.
- C4 at (1012, 720), double-bonded to C5.
- N3 at (1080, 797), the unprotonated N, single-bonded to C4.
- C2 at (1030, 882), double-bonded to N3.
- N1, labelled HN, at about (910, 862), single-bonded to C2 and to C5.

SMILES: CC(c1cncn1)c1cccc(C)c1C

Check on the written SMILES: `c1cncn1` starts at C5 (the attachment atom, c1), then c (C4), n (N3), c (C2), n1 (NH). The N written as the last atom needs an H, so the 1H form should be `c1c[nH]cn1` or equivalently `c1cnc[nH]1`. Here C5 is bonded to the NH, so I use `c1cnc[nH]1`.

SMILES: CC(c1cnc[nH]1)c1cccc(C)c1C

name: ctl_135

name: ctl_136
text:
The image shows a corticosteroid: a 6-methyl-1,4-dien-3-one steroid (methylprednisolone type) with an 11-hydroxyl, a 17-propionate ester and a 21-acetate ester.

**Ring A:** The 3-ketone sits on a cross-conjugated 1,4-diene. The C1=C2 and C4=C5 double bonds are both drawn.

**Substituents:**
- C6 carries a methyl.
- C10 and C13 carry methyls.
- C11 carries an OH.
- C17 carries an OC(=O)CH2CH3 group (propionate) and a C(=O)CH2OC(=O)CH3 side chain (21-acetate).

**Stereochemistry:** The ring system is drawn flipped vertically relative to the usual steroid orientation, with ring A's C1=C2 at the bottom. After accounting for that flip, the C10 and C13 methyls and the 11-OH are on the β face, the C17 propionate is on the α face, and the 6-methyl is α. This matches the natural steroid configuration of 6α-methylprednisolone. The wedge on the C7–C8 bond is ambiguous in the drawing, so I took C8 as the natural 8β-H.

I built the SMILES from the known methylprednisolone SMILES and substituted the 17-propionate and 21-acetate groups. This keeps the neighbour order at each stereocentre, so the @/@@ marks carry over unchanged.

SMILES: C[C@H]1C[C@H]2[C@@H]3CC[C@@]([C@]3(C[C@@H]([C@@H]2[C@@]4(C1=CC(=O)C=C4)C)O)C)(C(=O)COC(C)=O)OC(=O)CC

name: ctl_132

I read this structure as lenacapavir and wrote the SMILES region by region from the drawing.

**Fragments read from the image**

- **Cyclopentane:** it carries a CF2 and is fused to a cyclopropane. The two wedges at the ring fusion give the cyclopropane carbons `[C@@H]` (the one bonded to CF2) and `[C@H]` (the one bonded to the pyrazole carbon).

name: ctl_125
text:
I read the molecule as a 14-membered macrolide ketolide with a fused five-membered lactone, a desosamine sugar, and an amidoxime side chain ending in a thiadiazolyl-pyridine. Stereochemistry is taken from the wedges and hashes, but some of it is uncertain.

- **Macrocycle:** the ring runs from the lactone C=O through CH(CH3), a ketone, CH(CH3), CH(O-sugar), C(CH3)(OCH3), CH2, CH(CH3), a second ketone, CH(CH3), and a ring-fusion CH. It then passes through the quaternary C(CH3) and CH(ethyl) and closes back through the ring O to the lactone C=O.
- **Fused lactone:** the quaternary C(CH3) carries an O that goes to a C(=O), which attaches to the CH bearing the side chain. This closes a γ-butyrolactone with the ring-fusion CH.
- **Side chain:** a C(NH2)=N–O amidoxime, with the O attached to CH(CH3) bearing a 1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-yl group, which is substituted at C5 with 2-pyridyl. From the drawing, the oxime O is trans to the ring CH across C=N.
- **Sugar:** a desosamine unit, drawn as a tetrahydropyran with 6-CH3, 4-N(CH3)2 and 3-OH, linked through the glycosidic O.

The wedge/hash pattern at the quaternary C(CH3) and the neighbouring ring-fusion CH is ambiguous in the image. I assumed the methyl on the quaternary carbon is hashed and the bond to the ring-fusion CH is hashed from that CH. The other centres were assigned from their drawn wedges, hashes and neighbour positions.

SMILES: CC[C@H]1OC(=O)[C@H](C)C(=O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O[C@@H]3O[C@H](C)C[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H]3O)[C@](C)(OC)C[C@@H](C)C(=O)[C@H](C)[C@@H]2[C@]1(C)OC(=O)[C@H]2/C(N)=N/O[C@@H](C)c1nnc(s1)c1ccccn1

name: ctl_139
text:
The drawing looks like an ertugliflozin analogue, so I built the SMILES from the known ertugliflozin SMILES and changed the one substituent that differs. I did not independently re-derive the ring stereocentres from the wedges and hashes. I assumed they match ertugliflozin.

- **Aryl part:** a 4-chloro-3-(4-ethoxybenzyl)phenyl group (ethoxy on one ring, a CH2 bridge, then a chloro-substituted ring) is attached to the ketal carbon of the bicycle.
- **Bicycle:** a 6,8-dioxabicyclo[3.2.1]octane core with three OH groups on the carbocyclic ring, as in ertugliflozin.
- **Difference from ertugliflozin:** the bridgehead carbon bears a CH(OH)CH3 group instead of CH2OH.
- **Side-chain stereocentre:** the CH3 is on a wedge, the OH is on a plain bond, and the carbon is attached to the bridgehead. Using the priority order OH > bridgehead C > CH3, with H pointing away, this centre is R. That corresponds to `[C@@H](C)O` in the SMILES.

name: ctl_144
text:
The drawing shows decitabine (5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine). I read it in three parts.

**Base:** a six-membered 1,3,5-triazine ring with three ring nitrogens. It carries an NH2 group on one carbon and a C=O on the carbon between two ring nitrogens. The ring nitrogen next to the carbonyl is bonded to the sugar. One C=N double bond is drawn at the bottom of the ring and another on the left.

**Sugar:** a five-membered ring (four carbons plus the ring O) with no 2'-OH, so it is a 2'-deoxyribose. The 3'-carbon carries an OH drawn with a hashed bond. The 4'-carbon carries a CH2OH drawn with a wedge.

**Stereochemistry:** the bond from C1' to the base nitrogen is a wedge. This wedge/hash/wedge pattern is the β-D-2'-deoxyribose configuration. I took the stereo descriptors from the standard 2'-deoxycytidine SMILES (recalled, not recomputed), since the sugar is drawn the same way and only the base differs.

SMILES: NC1=NC(=O)N(C=N1)[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](CO)O1

name: ctl_141
text:
This is cefepime. I read it region by region:

- **Bicyclic core:** a cephem, with a β-lactam fused to a six-membered ring containing S. The ring C=C carries a carboxylate (COO⁻) on one carbon and a CH2 substituent on the other.
- **C3 substituent:** a CH2 attached to an N-methylpyrrolidinium (N⁺ in a five-membered ring, bearing a methyl).
- **C7 side chain:** an amide NH–C(=O)–C(=N–OCH3) bearing a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl ring.
- **Ring stereocentres:** the two wedges at C6 and C7 give the (6R,7R) configuration. Working through the neighbour order at each centre, I get `[C@H]` for C7 and `[C@@H]` for C6 in the SMILES below.
- **Oxime geometry:** I took this as Z, the known configuration of cefepime, rather than deriving it independently from the drawing.

name: ctl_148
text:
This is merbromin (mercurochrome): a dibromofluorescein core carrying a Hg+ substituent, drawn with two Na+ counterions and a hydroxide.

**Xanthene core.** The left ring has these substituents:
- Br at the top-left carbon.
- O⁻ at the lower-left carbon.
- Hg⁺ at the bottom carbon, next to the ring-fusion carbon that bears the bridging O.

The right ring has Br at the top-right carbon and a C=O (ketone) at the lower right. The central ring contains the bridging O and the C9 carbon, which carries the aryl group.

**Aryl group.** The pendant benzene ring has a carboxylate (C(=O)[O-]) ortho to the point where it joins C9.

**Counterions.** Two Na+ and one HO⁻ are drawn as separate species.

**Writing the SMILES.** I start at the carboxylate and go through the aryl ring to C9:
[O-]C(=O)c1ccccc1C2=C3C=C(Br)C(=O)C=C3Oc4c2cc(Br)c([O-])c4[Hg+]

Checking the ring bonds:
- Right ring: C9=C3 (C9 double-bonded to a ring-fusion carbon), then C=C(Br)C(=O)C=C3, with C3 closing the ring. The ring atoms are C3 (fusion), CH, C(Br), C(=O), CH, and C3' (the other fusion carbon, bonded to O). I wrote `C3C=C(Br)C(=O)C=C3O`, so the first C3 opens the ring, then C=, C(Br), C(=O), C=, and the final C3 closes it. That makes the ring members C3a, CH, CBr, C=O, CH, C3b, which is 6 atoms. C3b is attached to O, and the final `C=C3` is a C=C bond, so C3b is double-bonded to the preceding CH. The ring is C3a(=C9)–CH=C(Br)... wait, `C=C(Br)` makes CH=CBr, so C3a–CH is a single bond, which is fine.
- Left ring: c4 (attached to O), c2 (fusion carbon bonded to C9, written `c2` to close the ring-2 label), then cc(Br)c([O-])c4[Hg+]. The ring atoms are c4(O), c2(C9), cH, c(Br), c(O⁻), c(Hg), which is 6 atoms. The last atom, c(Hg), closes to c4, so Hg sits adjacent to the carbon bearing the bridging O. This matches the drawing.

Adding the counterions gives the full SMILES.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[OH-].[O-]C(=O)c1ccccc1C2=C3C=C(Br)C(=O)C=C3Oc4c2cc(Br)c([O-])c4[Hg+]

name: ctl_143
text:
This is the isavuconazonium cation, with the 2,5-difluorophenyl carbinol and the 4-(4-cyanophenyl)thiazole core. I read it in these parts:

- **Left chain:** a sarcosine ester (CH3NHCH2C(=O)O–CH2–) is attached at the 3-position of a pyridine. The pyridine 2-position carries N(CH3)–C(=O)–O–CH(CH3)–.
- **Triazolium:** the CH(CH3) group sits on the N+ of a 1,2,4-triazolium. The ring N at the other end is bonded to a CH2.
- **Central chain:** CH2 leads to a quaternary carbon bearing OH (hashed bond) and the 2,5-difluorophenyl ring. Next is a CH bearing a CH3 (wedged bond) and the thiazol-2-yl group.
- **Thiazole:** its 4-position carries a 4-cyanophenyl group.

**Stereochemistry:**
- The CH(CH3) carbon has priorities thiazolyl > C(OH) > CH3 > H. With the methyl wedged and H behind, the sequence runs clockwise, so it is R.
- The carbinol carbon has priorities OH > CH2N > aryl > CH(CH3). With the OH hashed, this works out to R.
- This matches the known (2R,3R) configuration of isavuconazonium.
- The CH(CH3) carbon between the triazolium N+ and the carbamate oxygen is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

SMILES: C[C@@H](c1nc(cs1)-c1ccc(C#N)cc1)[C@](O)(Cn1c[n+](C(C)OC(=O)N(C)c2ncccc2COC(=O)CNC)cn1)c1cc(F)ccc1F

name: ctl_149
text:
I read the drawing as three pieces joined together:

- **Left:** a morpholine ring (O at the far left, N on the right) attached through its nitrogen to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Centre:** that benzene ring carries an NH on the opposite side, which connects to C8 of an imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazine core. In this core, N7 sits next to C8, C6 bears the aryl group, C5 is an unsubstituted CH, and N4 is the bridgehead nitrogen.
- **Bottom:** the substituent on C6 is a 1H-indazole. Its NH (N1) is bonded to C7a, and C3a bonds to C3 (the CH next to N2). The carbon bonded to the pyrazine is adjacent to C7, which makes it C6 of the indazole, so the group is indazol-6-yl.

No wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry are drawn, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

I traced the ring closures atom by atom against the drawing: the imidazopyrazine closure `c23` joins C8a back to C8 and N4, and the indazole path runs C6, C5, C4, C3a, C3, N2, N1H, C7a, C7.

name: ctl_150
text:
The image shows five separate carbon monoxide units and one Fe atom, with no bonds between them. Each CO is drawn as C with a lone pair, a triple bond (shown as two lines plus a dash) and O. This is iron pentacarbonyl drawn as disconnected fragments.

Each CO is drawn as [C]#O with a lone pair on carbon, which corresponds to the neutral carbon monoxide form [C-]#[O+]. Written as a disconnected-component SMILES, the drawing is five CO fragments plus Fe:

[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[Fe]

The charges are not drawn in the image. Writing the carbons as C with a lone pair and a triple bond to O gives `[C]#O`, or simply `C#O` with implicit hydrogens, which would be wrong. I use the charge-separated form because it is the valid way to represent CO.

SMILES: [C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[Fe]

name: ctl_147
text:
I read the molecule as a bis(2-chloroethyl)phosphorodiamidate ester attached to the anomeric carbon of a pyranose ring.

**Phosphorus part:** P carries a P=O, two NH–CH2CH2Cl arms, and a single-bonded O that links to the ring.

**Ring:** it is a six-membered ring of five carbons plus one ring oxygen. The ring carbons, going around from the anomeric carbon, are:
- C1 (anomeric): O–P on a bold wedge.
- C2: OH on a hashed bond.
- C3: OH on a bold wedge.
- C4: OH on a hashed bond.
- C5: CH2OH on a bold wedge.

**Stereochemistry:** I worked out each centre's @/@@ from the 2D positions of its neighbours. The implicit H is placed opposite the wedge or hash. I then adjusted for the atom order in the SMILES string.

**Check:** the string has one ring closure (the pyranose ring), P with =O, two N substituents and one O, and two CH2CH2Cl chains. This matches the drawing atom for atom.
